subject: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Hi Ava — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I put together three practical reserved-commit packages for Velora with suggested GPU pool sizing, ramp cadence, and the tradeoffs on start windows and SLA credits. High-level: 12/24/36 month term options, with steeper discounts for longer commitments and an optional accelerated ramp for a higher near-term utilization guarantee.

Summary (attachments: Initial_Pricing_Deck-Velora.pdf):
- Sizing assumptions: baseline workload peaks at ~2,000 reqs/sec with 150ms p95 target; steady-state average 900–1,100 reqs/sec. We modeled this as ~40–56 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on batching/quantization choices.
- Term options (examples):
  * 12-month: baseline discount, standard ramp (full capacity by month 6).
  * 24-month: ~12% across-the-board discount vs 12m, can move to month-4 full capacity.
  * 36-month: ~20% discount vs 12m, option to accelerate to full capacity by month 3 with an up-front commitment sizing clause.
- Ramp windows: standard ramp (25% month1, 50% month2, 75% month3, 100% month6). Accelerated ramp pushes 100% by month3 but requires commit of >=80% of reserved capacity in month1.
- Start window: we can hold the reserved pool for up to a 90-day start window from execution; beyond that we ask to shift the commit or accept a reduced guaranteed throughput until activation.
- SLA credits: default SLA includes monthly credits for missed latency SLOs (examples in deck). For firm commercial guarantees and lower p95 targets we can include stronger credits or financial thresholds.

Questions for you:
1) Do you need firm start-by date constraints (e.g., must begin by 2026-07-15)?
2) Is Velora ok with the 80% month-1 commit if you want the accelerated ramp on a 36-month term?
3) Are burst/buffer policies required (short spikes beyond committed throughput)? We support burst pools but they are metered separately or as a negotiated burst allowance.

I attached a short spreadsheet with line-item showed in the deck (Commit_Summary_VEL-3741.xlsx) and a draft MSA to accelerate legal review. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0121

From: Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <m.patel@velora.ai>, procurement@velora.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Tessa — thanks, useful. A few clarifying items from our end before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Start date: we were hoping to push to a July 15 start. Can you confirm the 90-day hold and whether there are fees if we miss that?
2) SLA: our app requires a firm 150ms p95 under committed throughput. If Redwood can't meet that we need a clear financial remedy (not just credits). Can you map the SLA tiers to dollar credits?
3) Burst: we expect occasional spikes up to ~3,000 reqs/sec for short windows (5–10 minutes). How is burst priced and does it impact committed capacity?
4) Invoice cadence: procurement prefers quarterly invoices. Any preference or constraint there?

One more: can you call out how you define 'reserved capacity' (GPU-hours/month vs reserved top-line throughput)? Procurement will need that spelled out.

If you can send a quick one-pager addressing those 4 bullets we'll route internally and loop legal.

—Ava
Ava Reynolds, Head of ML Platform, Velora AI

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Ava — hi, Ben here (sales ops). Quick answers and a concrete pricing table attached. See Commit_Summary_VEL-3741.xlsx for line-by-line. Short version: 

- Definition: reserved capacity = committed GPU-hours per month (we convert to effective throughput using model profile + avg seq length). We can alternatively contract on a reserved RPS band, but our standard commercial unit is GPU-hours for predictable scheduling and isolation.

- Start hold/fees: 90-day hold is standard and no extra fee if you start within that window. If start is delayed >90 days, we roll down the committed guarantee by 10% per 30 days past the window unless you pay a storage/retainer equivalent (we can call that a "hold fee").

- Burst: we provide a burst pool tied to the Dedicated instance class. Short bursts are allowed; any sustained burst beyond negotiated buffer is billed at on-demand rates. Example: short spike up to +30% of committed throughput for <15 minutes/day is free; anything above that negotiated separately.

- SLA credits mapping:
  * If monthly p95 latency for committed traffic exceeds target, we issue a 5% credit of committed monthly fee for first breach, 10% for second in same quarter, and escalation thereafter (we're flexible on thresholds).
  * For a stronger commercial remedy (e.g., dollar-based service credits or termination rights), we can add explicit language in the SOW / MSA.

- Pricing examples (all $k/month committed spend equivalents, illustrative):
  * 12-month: baseline rate = $190k/month (no accelerated ramp).
  * 24-month: 12% off baseline = $167k/month with standard ramp or $160k/month if you accept month-1 at 80% committed for fast ramp.
  * 36-month: 20% off baseline = $152k/month; with accelerated ramp (full by month3) require 80% month-1 commit; additional 2% off if invoice quarterly in advance.

Links: https://redwood.example.com/deals/VEL-3741 (pricing materials) and DocuSign preview: https://docusign.example.com/preview/VEL-3741. Attached: Commit_Summary_VEL-3741.xlsx and draft MSA.

If these numbers look directionally right we can convert the 36-month scenario into a countersigned SOW with the ramp table explicit and a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Ben

From: Maya Patel <m.patel@velora.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>, procurement@velora.ai
Date: 2026-06-24T11:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Ben/Tessa — procurement questions (quick):

1) The 36-month with accelerated ramp looks attractive on price, but we can only agree to accelerated month-1 commitment if we have certainty on the start date. Our window target: start no later than 2026-07-15. If Redwood misses that, we need either (a) a pro-rated credit equal to 100% of lost committed hours until activation or (b) the option to shift to a shorter term without penalty. Which can you accept?

2) SLA: the p95 150ms requirement is non-negotiable under committed traffic. We need a dollar-based remedy: propose 10% monthly credit for each breach and a 30-day cure period; after second breach in 12 months, customer may terminate with limited liability. Please confirm willingness to move from percentage credits to dollar credits and provide an example calculation.

3) Burst: our calendar includes a product launch on 2026-10-01 with expected spikes. We need a guaranteed burst allowance (up to +50% for 30 minutes/day) included in the SOW for the first 6 months only.

4) Invoice cadence: quarterly billing OK, prefer net-45 payment terms.

If Redwood can accept (a) start-by 2026-07-15 or the pro-rated credit option, (b) a dollar-credit SLA mapping for p95, and (c) the 6-month burst allowance, procurement will greenlight legal review.

Thanks,
Maya (Procurement Lead, Velora)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <m.patel@velora.ai>, Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, procurement@velora.ai
Date: 2026-06-25T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Maya — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Proposal from Redwood to move forward (negotiation compromise):

1) Start date and hold: We can commit to a firm start-by 2026-07-15 if the SOW is signed and the month-1 invoice is accepted by Velora no later than 2026-07-01. If Redwood misses the activation date due to infra issues on our side, Redwood will provide a pro-rated credit equal to the portion of reserved GPU-hours not delivered in that month (this is effectively the 100% credit you requested).

2) SLA dollars: We will convert the percentage credit model into a dollar-based remedy tied to committed monthly fee. Example: for a $152k committed month (36m tier), a p95 breach = $15,200 credit (10% of committed fee). First breach: 10% credit; second breach in same 12-month period: 20% credit; after second breach customer may terminate with limited liability (we'll add a 30-day cure period). We'll draft specific language for the MSA/SOW.

3) Burst allowance: we will include a guaranteed burst allowance of +50% for up to 30 minutes/day for months 1–6. Any sustained burst beyond that will be billed at agreed on-demand rates.

4) Invoice cadence & terms: Quarterly invoices are fine; Redwood standard net-30, we can accept net-45 for enterprise procurement. If Velora prepays quarterly in advance we can apply an additional 2% credit on the committed fee.

5) Accelerated ramp: Redwood will accept the 36-month accelerated ramp (100% by month3) if Velora commits to >=80% of reserved capacity in month1 and agrees to the invoicing cadence noted above. 

Next step: I will have Legal prepare the SOW language reflecting the start-by date, the pro-rated credit clause, SLA dollar credits, and the 6-month burst allowance. Ben will send an updated Excel pricing table and a DocuSign envelope for an execution path.

If this matches Velora's ask we'll schedule a short finalization call later this week.

Best,
Tessa

From: Ava Reynolds <ava@velora.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <m.patel@velora.ai>, procurement@velora.ai
Date: 2026-06-25T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserved-commit: sizing, start window & SLA tradeoffs

Tessa/Ben — that all looks reasonable. Procurement will circulate the revised SOW language once Ben sends the updated pricing sheet and DocuSign. We agree in principle to the 36-month accelerated ramp with 80% month-1 commit, quarterly invoices (prefer net-45), and the SLA dollar-credit structure you proposed.

I'll set up a 30-minute call for Thursday 2026-06-26 to finalize signatures and the exact invoicing cadence. Thanks for moving quickly.

—Ava
